title: Single electrons build interference one dot at a time
body: Fire electrons at two slits so sparsely that they arrive one by one, and each lands as a single dot, yet thousands of dots gradually draw interference bands. Tonomura's 1989 filmed experiment shows statistics becoming pattern with no electron ever 'splitting' visibly. The mathematics says amplitude interferes; the screen says dots. Both are the data.
source_hint: Tonomura et al. (1989), electron biprism experiment
